item.title: 2 ships attacked in Strait of Hormuz as Trump grapples with his next move
item.description: Following more attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, Trump said he'll make a "big decision" on whether to "annihilate" Iran's leadership.

item.title: Increased ICE enforcement in 2025 hurt local employment, analysis finds
item.description: Employment fell last year in U.S. cities where ICE arrests surged, according to the Brookings Institution.

item.title: Police capture suspected serial killer disguised as woman, carrying baby
item.description: Brazilian police said they will reopen dozens of cases linked to a self-confessed serial killer who was arrested as he attempted to escape dressed as a woman and carrying a baby.

item.title: Trump to sign Russia sanctions bill today, source says
item.description: President Trump will sign the recently passed Russia sanctions bill Friday, a White House official tells CBS News. CBS News' Weijia Jiang has more on that and the rest of the news coming out of the White House.

item.title: AI agent Claude is building the next version of itself, Anthropic says
item.description: Anthropic says AI agent Claude is building the next version of itself as industry experts continue to sound alarms about the technology's potential power and risks. Journalist and author Sebastian Mallaby joins CBS News to discuss his new op-ed saying calls by Anthropic co-founder Dario Amodei to slow down AI development don't go far enough.

item.title: Grandmother falsely accused of bank fraud sues Fargo, North Dakota, over AI facial recognition
item.description: A Tennessee grandmother is suing the city of Fargo, North Dakota, after facial recognition software linked her to a crime she didn't commit, which led to a nearly six-month stay in jail. CBS News' Nicole Valdes has more.

item.title: Unpacking GOP Rep. Salazar's ad blasting Trump's immigration policies
item.description: Only six weeks remain before Americans vote in November's midterm elections. CBS News' Zak Hudak has the latest political headlines.

item.title: Flights are only going to get more expensive so book your holiday tickets now, expert says
item.description: Travel costs are up as fuel prices soar. The Points Guys managing editor Clint Henderson shares his cost saving tips.

item.title: Uber ordered to pay $40 million in wrongful death suit
item.description: A woman was hit and killed after an Uber driver forced her and her friend out of his car on a freeway. Now, Uber has been ordered to pay $40 million after the victim's family brought forth a wrongful death suit. CBS News' Lauren Pozen reports.

item.title: Why Gold Star families are still seeking answers after deadly Kuwait attack
item.description: In a reporter's notebook, CBS News correspondent Jonah Kaplan details his series of exclusive stories on an Iranian drone strike that hit a U.S. military facility at the Port of Shuaiba, Kuwait, on March 1, 2026. Six U.S. service members were killed and dozens were injured — raising questions about what the Pentagon has told the American public about the attack and leaving families searching for answers.

item.title: FAA says Trump arch will not interfere with D.C. airport flight path
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration approved President Trump's plans for a triumphal arch across the Potomac River from Washington, D.C.

item.title: FAA says Trump arch will not interfere with D.C. airport flight path
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration on Friday said President Trump's planned triumphal arch next to Arlington Cemetery and near the Lincoln Memorial poses no hazard to flights coming into and departing from Washington Reagan National Airport.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Sept. 20)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Trump's next move could be to "annihilate" Iran, he tells Axios
item.description: President Trump told Axios that his next move could be to "annihilate" Iran. CBS News' Aaron Navarro reports.

item.title: Director explains how "feeling freaked out" about AI motivated his filmmaking
item.description: Expert whistleblowers and frontier tech CEOs are calling for government oversight and boundaries for artificial intelligence development after a series of incidents where AI agents went rogue. Director Daniel Roher explains how conversations around AI motivated him to make "The AI Doc: Or How I Became an Apocaloptimist."

item.title: Use of AI backfires on an expert witness at trial: "They have biases"
item.description: The use of artificial intelligence in the courtroom is drawing fresh attention after an expert witness in a multimillion-dollar lawsuit used ChatGPT to help create his report.

item.title: Duncan Sheik, singer-songwriter of "Barely Breathing," dies at 56
item.description: Duncan Sheik died on Thursday night, his family said.

item.title: Congregation returns to Michigan synagogue for first time since terror attack
item.description: The congregation at Michigan's Temple Israel is returning for the first time since the synagogue was targeted in a terror attack.

item.title: High-stakes debates world leaders will have at U.N. General Assembly
item.description: World leaders will gather in New York City next week for the U.N. General Assembly, with several heads of state and other government officials expected to speak, including President Trump. The gathering will feature several days of high-level debates on global issues. Here's what to expect.

item.title: Trump touts plan for new U.S. base as Poland warns of risks from Russia
item.description: Trump touts "major progress" on plans for a permanent U.S. Army base in Poland as the country's leader warns Russia's war on Ukraine could hit NATO soil.

item.title: Twins conjoined at the head are separated in 25-hour surgery
item.description: The twins were born in Ethiopia with a rare condition that left them joined at the head. Doctors spent a year planning a separation surgery.

item.title: Analyzing the fight over AI regulations
item.description: Patrick McGee, a contributing writer for The Free Press, says AI firms "are not jogging...they're still sprinting" despite agreeing to pace the frontier. Here's the latest.

item.title: Doctor reacts after RFK Jr. tells anti-vax group they have "a friend at the White House"
item.description: Health and Human Service Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. spoke at a conference for Children's Health Defense, an anti-vaccine activism group he helped lead years ago. CBS News medical correspondent Dr. Céline Gounder shares her reaction.

item.title: New shocking claims from Princess Diana's brother
item.description: The brother of the late Princess Diana claims in his upcoming book that then Prince Charles sounded upbeat after his ex-wife died in a Paris car crash in 1997. When asked about these allegations, Buckingham Palace referred to a statement it released earlier this week saying that the king "is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgement and colour memory, even many years after such a loss." Watch more of Charles Spencer interview only on "CBS Sunday Morning."

item.title: Holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy trial says he "didn't have any doubts"
item.description: Michael Desronvil, the lone holdout juror in the high-profile Lindsay Clancy murder trial, said he "didn't have any doubts" during deliberations.

item.title: Senator urges Trump to press Xi on Chinese info Iran may be using to target troops
item.description: Democratic Sen. Elissa Slotkin urged President Trump to make this issue a "centerpiece of your talks with President Xi."

item.title: Michigan synagogue reopens 6 months after terror attack
item.description: Temple Israel, a Detroit-area synagogue, has spent the last six months rebuilding after a terror attack destroyed parts of the building.

item.title: Princess Diana's brother claims Prince Charles seemed "upbeat" after she died
item.description: The brother of the late Princess Diana claims in his upcoming book that then Prince Charles seemed "upbeat" right after his ex-wife died in a Paris car crash in 1997. When asked about these allegations, Buckingham Palace referred to a statement it released earlier this week saying that the king "is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgement and colour memory, even many years after such a loss." Watch more of Charles Spencer's conversation with Mark Phillips on "CBS Sunday Morning."

item.title: Trump photo shows him viewing "Kennedy Center demolished" document
item.description: In court documents filed Wednesday by Rep. Joyce Beatty, a witness said he saw a "forklift run into and hit the pillars" of the building.
